subject: SLA Template: Operational tolerance, baseline uptime & credit trigger workflow

From: laura_bennett

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA Template: Operational tolerance, baseline uptime & credit trigger workflow

Hi Evan —

Following our call this morning, attaching a first-pass SLA template rather than the redline. Keys I want to get aligned on before legal sees anything:

- Baseline availability: 99.95% monthly across hosted regions (measured at platform ingress).
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 250ms for standard gen endpoints; separate band for batched/offline inference.
- Exception carveouts: scheduled maintenance (72-hour rolling window notice), customer-driven load spikes (documented burst patterns), and cross-region failover events.
- Credit trigger workflow: credits scale by monthly availability shortfall; separate small partial credit for sustained latency regressions.
- Credit cap: proposing a hard cap at 25% of monthly invoice as a guardrail — want to confirm this is acceptable to you.

Attached: SLA_template_draft_20280618.pdf and an uptime-metrics-matrix.xlsx (mapping p95/p99 and measurement points). Would like to agree on definitions for "downtime" vs "degradation" and a process for submitting an exception request (who at TideRidge should own that).

Next steps I propose:
1) You flag any carveouts we missed and confirm the max-credit cap.
2) We agree the latency threshold and whether we should offer latency-only credits (partial credits when p95 > X for >Y hours).
3) If that looks OK, we route to procurement for the DocuSign flow.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA_template_draft_20280618.pdf (application/pdf), uptime-metrics-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the draft. A few quick reactions from TideRidge:

- EU regional requirement: we need an EU-region-specific availability baseline of 99.9% for the first 6 months of the contract while we complete our certification run. Can you accommodate a temporary regional uplift exception?
- Credit cap: 25% is reasonable as a starting point but procurement will want an explicit monthly escrow process for partial credits (to avoid retroactive billing complications).
- Latency credits: we prefer a layered approach — partial credit if p95 > 350ms for >= 8 consecutive hours, full credit bands for availability breaches only.

We're looping procurement on this thread for the documented exception flow and to kick off the PO process.

On manufacturing of burst patterns — we'll share a CSV with hour-by-hour traffic for the last 90 days (that should help you tune the batched-inference carveout).

Regards,
Evan
VP Product, TideRidge

Thanks Evan — tagging a couple of operational details so we can be precise in the doc:

- Measurement point: availability will be measured at the API gateway in the region handling the request; we'll list the exact URL endpoints and synthetic checks in the appendix.
- Degradation vs outage: "degradation" = >= 10% error rate or p95 latency crossing threshold for >30m; "outage" = >= 50% error rate or total ingress failure.
- Exception request process: customer opens a ticket in our portal with the "SLA Exception" tag, we have a 48-hour triage SLA internally and a 5-business-day investigation window.

I'll draft the short procedural paragraph to drop into the SLA and add an example exception workflow for scheduled region migration.

Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference

Quick note from finance/ops perspective:

- I approve a maximum monthly credit cap of 25% of the invoice (LAURA — confirm we include language that caps cumulative credits in any invoice cycle).
- For latency-only credits, propose the following: when p95 > 500ms for a sustained 6-hour window, a small partial credit equal to 5% of the pro-rata daily charge for affected endpoints. This preserves incentives for both sides.
- Suggest adding a hard upper bound on combined credits over the first 3 months at 40% to protect for migration risk.

If TideRidge is OK with those boundaries, we can include explicit formulae in the SLA (example: credit = min(25% * monthly_invoice, calculated_shortfall_amount)).

Aditya Rao
VP, Revenue Operations
